definition: Metamorphosis means a complete change of form or character.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word metamorphosis. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know metamorphosis should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Friends from her quiet suburb barely recognized the woman on stage; the metamorphosis from shy bookkeeper to headlining comic had taken six years of open mics.
An adjustment is far milder than a metamorphosis — a nudge to one setting, with the thing itself left untouched.
A makeover is milder than a metamorphosis — it freshens the surface, while a metamorphosis rebuilds the creature underneath.

An overhaul is a thorough, deliberate rebuild — an engine or a curriculum taken apart and put back better — that stops short of changing what the thing is. A metamorphosis crosses that line: after it, the before and after barely share a skeleton.

A rebirth is a fresh start — the emphasis is renewal, a thing alive again, more than any change in what it looks like or is. Metamorphosis stresses altered form: the shape or character has been rebuilt so completely that the original is hard to find.

Reinvention is what people, brands, and careers do to themselves on purpose — a deliberate remaking of image or direction. A metamorphosis needs no intent and no self: a landscape, an institution, or a timid clerk can undergo one, and the word measures the astonishing distance crossed.
